newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan business seeks unity against Sandinistas.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan business seeks unity against Sandinistas.

text.p: Nicaragua's largest business group on Tuesday asked voters to back rightist Arnoldo Aleman in the October 20 presidential election to stop the left-wing Sandinistas from returning to power.

"The Sandinista Front is not capable of generating the confidence necessary for the private sector and foreign and national investment," a statement issued by the Higher Council of Private Enterprise (COSEP) said.
It said a Sandinista government was "totally unacceptable" given the "damage" they had caused to the country.

While other Nicaraguan business leaders have warned that a Sandinista victory would scare off investors, this was the first public statement against the Sandinistas by COSEP, which represents a large part of Nicaragua's private sector.

The Sandinistas, whose candidate is former President Daniel Ortega, governed Nicaragua from 1979 to 1990 with Soviet and Cuban backing, confiscating private property and introducing a planned economy.
The Sandinistas have changed their image in the current campaign, selling themselves as a moderate, centre-left party that would respect private property and the free market.
But the COSEP statement showed that much of Nicaragua's business sector distrusts the Sandinista conversion.
COSEP called on voters to unite "to avoid a return of the Sandinista Front and strengthen the candidate who the serious polling firms give a possibility of victory (Aleman)."
With five days to go to the election, polls give Aleman a slim lead over Ortega in a race that pollsters have said could go either way. More than 20 other candidates barely figure in the polls.
If no candidate wins at least 45 percent of the vote, a runoff between the top two candidates would be held in late November or early December.
